definition: Relegate means to assign to a lower or less important position.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word relegate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know relegate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: After one shaky rehearsal, the first-chair violinist found herself relegated to the back of the section.
Overlook is milder than relegate — nobody assigns you anywhere when you are overlooked; you are simply not chosen this time, while relegate hands you a lower place on purpose.
Banish goes further than relegate — a relegated player still suits up, lower on the roster, while a banished one is off the team and out the door entirely.

To demote is to drop someone a rank at work — the plain paperwork word for a fall in job title. Relegate reaches far wider: people, dishes, columns, and whole teams can all be filed downward, and the new assignment always carries a sting of judgment.

To sideline someone is to push them out of the action while keeping them on hand — benched, but still in uniform. Relegate goes a step further: it assigns a definite lower place, a worse address everyone can see, and the judgment travels with it.

For forty years, the Gazette's weather report owned the top right corner of the front page.
Readers planned harvests and weddings around it.
The new owners, chasing clicks, relegated it to page nine, below the shipping notices, and gave its old corner to celebrity news.
The move was not an accident of layout.
An internal memo called the report a relic to be tucked away where it can do no harm.
Subscribers noticed the judgment in the new address, and hundreds canceled within a month -- many naming the page number in their letters.
